summary: CMS Property Management is a full-service residential property manager headquartered at 33 Brunswick Woods Drive in East Brunswick, NJ, handling single-family homes, condos, townhomes and small multifamily rentals for owners and investors across eight New Jersey counties. It runs on AppFolio owner and resident portals (online rent, maintenance requests, statements) and publishes its fee schedule: 10% of monthly rent for full service, one month's rent for leasing only, 50% of first month's rent for placement. The business reports a 4.5 rating from 116 Google reviews, and public reviews split between praise for statement clarity and portal access and complaints about difficulty reaching staff.

facts.fact: Services: marketing, tenant screening, leasing, rent collection, maintenance coordination, monthly owner financial statements, eviction coordination for single-family homes, condos, townhomes and small multifamily properties.

Office address is 33 Brunswick Woods Dr., East Brunswick, NJ 08816; phone (732) 838-3000; email info@cmspm.com; hours Monday-Friday 9:00 AM-5:00 PM; inquiries directed to a web form plus phone and email.
Published fee schedule: full-service management 10% of monthly rent; leasing only one month's rent; tenant placement 50% of first month's rent.
Operates as a licensed New Jersey real estate brokerage and holds security deposits in a NJ interest-bearing trust account.
Tenants pay rent and submit repair requests through an AppFolio resident portal (bank transfer or card, autopay); owners use an AppFolio owner portal; emergencies are also expected to be phoned in.
Site reports a 4.5 rating from 116 Google reviews and displays Trustindex-verified Google reviews on its testimonials page.
Service area spans eight counties (Essex, Hunterdon, Mercer, Middlesex, Monmouth, Ocean, Somerset, Union) with town counts per county, including 25 towns in Middlesex County.

Public AppFolio listings page showed about 17 active/vacant listings spread across North Brunswick, Somerville, South Plainfield, North Plainfield, Newark, Bloomingdale, Manville, Vauxhall, Jamesburg, Morganville, Old Bridge and Dunellen.
The site publishes town-level landing pages for well over 100 New Jersey municipalities plus an active blog of landlord-education articles.
Contact and owner pages still contain build notes such as a sample W-9 that 'carries over at production migration', indicating recent or in-progress website work.
A BBB directory search for the company name near East Brunswick returned 12 property-management results, none of them CMS Property Management.
SimplyHired shows no job listings under the name 'CMS Property Management' in East Brunswick, NJ or nationally.

operations_signals: Owner intake runs through a free-rental-analysis web form, a consultation scheduling link, phone (732) 838-3000 and info@cmspm.com — no online self-serve booking calendar or instant quote tool (https://www.cmspm.com/contact)

Office hours are Monday-Friday 9 AM-5 PM, but tenants are told to call emergencies in addition to logging the request, so after-hours coverage appears to be vendor triage rather than a staffed desk (https://www.cmspm.com/tenants)

All tenant/owner transactions — rent payment, autopay, maintenance requests, statements, lease and invoice documents — run through AppFolio portals, with online rental applications for vacant units (https://cmsproperty.appfolio.com/listings)

Lead-to-lease workflow is explicitly manual-sequence: rental analysis, owner approval of each placement, owner-set maintenance approval thresholds, and same-business-day inquiry responses promised (https://www.cmspm.com/new-jersey-property-management)

Municipal compliance work (rental registrations, smoke/CO inspections, lead-safe certifications for pre-1978 homes) is handled and tracked as part of full service — recurring deadline-driven admin (https://www.cmspm.com/owner-faq)

Service area is eight counties statewide with a single East Brunswick office, so showings, inspections and vendor coordination require remote scheduling across a wide geography (https://www.cmspm.com/)
Published pricing removes the custom-quote step but the site still pushes every visitor into a free rental analysis form or a call (https://www.cmspm.com/pricing)
hiring_signals: No careers or employment page exists on the site; /careers returns HTTP 404 (https://www.cmspm.com/careers)
No job listings found under the company name on SimplyHired for East Brunswick, NJ or nationally (https://www.simplyhired.com/search?q=%22cms+property+management%22&l=east+brunswick%2C+nj)
Company size and staffing are not disclosed anywhere on the site; the only named employees are staff mentioned in customer reviews (https://www.cmspm.com/testimonials)
review_themes: Positive: owners repeatedly credit clear, readable monthly statements and a portal with real-time numbers, framed as relief for out-of-state and busy owners (https://www.cmspm.com/testimonials)

Positive: maintenance coordination and HOA/tenant handling described as taking the landlord workload away; one reviewer specifically praised a named staff member's customer focus (https://www.cmspm.com/testimonials)
Positive: a remote owner with three properties said every detail is communicated and the portal has live data 24/7 (https://www.cmspm.com/testimonials)

Negative: a recurring tenant complaint is being unable to reach anyone or get a call back, with one review calling the company effectively an 'ai property management company' in feel and another saying things take too long (https://www.cmspm.com/testimonials)

Mixed: at least one owner flagged the maintenance fee charged per occurrence on top of the management percentage as high, while still rating the service positively (https://www.cmspm.com/testimonials)
Volume: the site claims 4.5 stars across 116 Google reviews, i.e. a substantial review base relative to a single-office manager (https://www.cmspm.com/)
tech_footprint: AppFolio is the core system of record: resident portal, owner portal, online applications, listing syndication and payment processing on cmsproperty.appfolio.com (https://cmsproperty.appfolio.com/listings)
Public listings run on AppFolio's listing engine with detail pages, amenity/utility/pet fields and photo galleries (https://cmsproperty.appfolio.com/listings)
Google Analytics 4 and a Google Ads/second property tag are installed sitewide (gtag G-VZ6ZZ66SRG and G-F82K75EFYL) (https://www.cmspm.com/contact)
WordPress site with a custom child theme, block-based templates and a programmatic sitemap of 100+ town landing pages (https://cmspm.com/wp-sitemap-posts-page-1.xml)
Trustindex review widget pulls verified Google reviews onto the testimonials page (https://www.cmspm.com/testimonials)
No live chat, chatbot, web scheduler or instant-estimate widget observed on the home, services, pricing or contact pages (https://www.cmspm.com/)
growth_signals: Footprint claimed across eight counties with county and town-level pages for 25 Middlesex towns, 53 Monmouth towns, 33 Ocean towns and more — an aggressive geographic content build-out (https://www.cmspm.com/)

Pricing page now publishes 10% full-service management, while a Google review from roughly six months earlier cited an 8% management fee plus $150 per maintenance occurrence — consistent with a recent repricing (https://www.cmspm.com/pricing)

Active listings extend well beyond the Middlesex core into Union, Somerset, Essex, Passaic and Morris County towns such as Newark, Vauxhall, North Plainfield, Somerville, Bloomingdale and Morganville (https://cmsproperty.appfolio.com/listings)

Blog cadence shows a burst of new content in late 2026 (landlord-tenant law, eviction process, landlord expenses) after a 2025 gap, alongside a whole-site redesign (https://cmspm.com/wp-sitemap-posts-post-1.xml)
Realtor referral program pays agents a one-time $500 fee per referred landlord client, an inbound-channel investment (https://www.cmspm.com/realtor-referral-program/)
decision_maker: Unknown — no owner, broker of record or GM is named on the site's home, about, contact, owner or agents pages, and LinkedIn/company-profile pages could not be accessed without being blocked (403).

inferences.inference: Management pricing was changed recently, from roughly 8% plus a per-occurrence maintenance fee to a flat 10% full-service rate.
inferences.reasoning: The published pricing page shows 10% with no per-occurrence fee, but a Google review of roughly six months earlier on their own testimonials page describes paying 8% plus $150 per maintenance occurrence.

inferences.inference: The biggest operational gap is inbound communication triage, not software.
inferences.reasoning: They already run AppFolio portals and promise same-business-day answers, yet the harshest reviews are about unreachable staff and unreturned calls, and there is no chat, scheduler or intake automation on the site — so routine status questions likely consume staff time.

inferences.inference: Volume is high enough that repetitive coordination work (applications, work-order updates, compliance deadlines, owner statements) is a meaningful cost center.
inferences.reasoning: 116 Google reviews, ~17 concurrent vacancies across a dozen towns, eight counties served from one office, and 100+ programmatic town pages all point to many parallel small transactions handled by a small single-office team.

inferences.inference: Hiring is likely informal or through personal networks rather than job boards.
inferences.reasoning: No careers page exists (404), and no postings appear under the company name on SimplyHired; absence of postings does not prove absence of hiring.

inferences.inference: The company is mid-migration on its website and likely receptive to tooling changes.
inferences.reasoning: Owner and tenant pages still carry internal build notes referencing a 'production migration', and dozens of town pages were modified within the same two-day window in November 2026.

inferences.inference: Tenant-side communication is probably handled by whoever is free rather than a dedicated line.
inferences.reasoning: Reviews both praise specific staff (e.g., a named coordinator) and complain that no one answers, which is typical of a lean office without a dedicated intake function.

data_gaps: Indeed, LinkedIn, ZipRecruiter, Yelp and Glassdoor blocked automated access (HTTP 403), so current/recent job postings and employee-count data could not be verified; no company careers page exists.
No BBB profile found for CMS Property Management near East Brunswick, so no BBB rating or complaint history is available.
Google review text and count were only observable through the company's own Trustindex-embedded reviews and its stated 4.5/116 figure; the Google Business Profile itself was not directly accessible.
No owner, broker of record or GM name found on any accessible company page; NJ real estate license lookup was not attempted because it requires an interactive form search.
Years in business could not be confirmed: the domain was parked in 2010-2016 archives and the earliest usable snapshot is 2021, and no 'since' date is published on the site.
Property count under management, revenue and headcount are not disclosed anywhere publicly accessible.
A single negative tenant review and one staff name in a positive review are the only tenant-side voices available; no other tenant review platform was reachable.
